title: Acids, Bases & Equilibrium
description: pH calculations, Brønsted–Lowry theory, buffers, Ka, Kc and Le Chatelier’s principle (all at 25 °C).

questions.text: Which of the following is a strong acid?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid dissociates essentially completely in water. Acetic acid, hydrofluoric acid and carbonic acid are all weak acids.

questions.text: What is the pH of a 0.010 M solution of $\ce{HCl}$?
questions.explanation: $\ce{HCl}$ is a strong acid, so $[\ce{H+}]$ = 0.010 M and pH = −log(0.010) = 2.00.

questions.text: What is the pH of a 0.0010 M solution of $\ce{NaOH}$ at 25 °C?
A buffer can be made by mixing a weak acid with its conjugate base.
questions.explanation: The weak acid neutralizes added base and its conjugate base neutralizes added acid, which resists large pH changes.

questions.text: Write the formula, including charge, of the conjugate base of $\ce{H2PO4-}$.
questions.explanation: A conjugate base is formed by removing one $\ce{H+}$. Removing $\ce{H+}$ from $\ce{H2PO4-}$ leaves $\ce{HPO4^{2-}}$.

questions.text: In $\ce{NH3 + H2O <=> NH4+ + OH-}$, select ALL species that act as Brønsted–Lowry acids (in either direction).
questions.explanation: A Brønsted–Lowry acid donates $\ce{H+}$. In the forward reaction $\ce{H2O}$ donates one; in the reverse reaction $\ce{NH4+}$ donates one. $\ce{NH3}$ and $\ce{OH-}$ accept protons, so they are bases.

questions.text: Match each solution (25 °C) to its approximate pH.
questions.explanation: 0.10 M strong acid: pH = −log(0.10) = 1. Pure water at 25 °C: pH = 7. 0.10 M strong base: pOH = 1, so pH = 13.

questions.text: Use the approximation $x = \sqrt{K_a C}$ to estimate $[\ce{H+}]$ in 0.100 M acetic acid ($K_a = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$).
For $\ce{2NO2 <=> N2O4}$, the equilibrium concentrations are $[\ce{NO2}]$ = 0.10 M and $[\ce{N2O4}]$ = 0.20 M. What is $K_c$?
For the exothermic reaction $\ce{N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3}$, which change shifts the equilibrium toward more $\ce{NH3}$?

options.text: Increasing the volume of the container (lower pressure)
Decreasing the volume of the container (higher pressure)

questions.explanation: The forward reaction converts 4 mol of gas into 2 mol, so higher pressure favors products. Heating an exothermic reaction and lowering the pressure both favor reactants, and a catalyst does not change the position of equilibrium.
